newsitem.title: singapore: Asia crudes mostly firmer, Oman falls, Minas flat.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes mostly firmer, Oman falls, Minas flat.

text.p: Asian crude prices were mostly firmer on Friday, mostly supported by stronger futures markets owing to the Iraqi tensions.
However, availability of Oman was undermining the crude with a U.S. major selling 500,000 barrels to a South Korean refiner at MPM minus nine cents per barrel.
That compared with the last deal done between a major and a separate South Korean refiner at MPM plus four cents earlier in September.
Traders said Oman lifting dates were pushing into the back end of October prompting some worries from the sellers.
Traders estimated at least four cargos were still available.
The crude futures rally pushed the Brent/Dubai spread wider to $2.20/$2.30 for November, out 10 cents from a day-earlier.
Dubai intermonths were steady, continuing this week's trend, at 40/45 cents per barrel for November/December and December/January.
A broker said a February/March Dubai spread was done at 39 cents late on Thursday.
Elsewhere in the physical market, a U.S. major sold 400,000 barrels of October Minas flat to the ICP. Another major said he sold Minas on Friday at ICP plus 10 cents to a major.
Minas has been in the doldrums for the past two trading months, falling as low as minus 70-90 cents on the differential.
In the light sweet market, 200,000 barrels of October Tapis were sold to a U.S. major at quotes plus 75 cents. A producer was asking well above $1.00 premium for October barrels.
Futures prices stayed firm with prompt Brent in London up 29 cents at $24.16, but still below the post Gulf War high hit on Thursday of $24.39.
